title: Bardziej, najbardziej
note: C1 Block 9, unit 4. Inbox item 11, deferred TWICE by name: a1_comparatives ('bardziej-comparatives and od+Gen deferred to A2') and then a2_superlatives, which fenced 'najbardziej + adjective' explicitly and paid only the od+Gen half. TWO NEW STRINGS, ZERO NEW ENDINGS: bardziej and najbardziej are invariable words that stand in front of an adjective which goes on agreeing exactly as it always did. THE DECISION RULE IS TAUGHT AS A TENDENCY OVER TWO CLOSED LISTS, NEVER AS A PRODUCTIVE TEST - the spine locks this and the b2_gen_pl_full fleeting-e precedent governs: this learner gets no value from a rule he cannot trust. List A = the NINE -szy comparatives he has owned since A1 (lepszy, gorszy, wiekszy, mniejszy, starszy, mlodszy, drozszy, tanszy, nowszy), which can NEVER take bardziej. List B = SIX owned adjectives that always do (zmeczony, zajety, chory, popularny, nowoczesny, skuteczny). Slide 4 says out loud that between the two lists Polish has adjectives which take the ending and are not in either list (trudniejszy from trudny), and that an unfamiliar adjective is to be CHECKED, not built - the same verified-never-coined discipline R2 imposed on prefixes. ANCHOR AND TRAP IN ONE WORD: bardzo is TAUGHT <- a2_directions_func [69] and has stood in front of adjectives since A2 (bardzo smaczna, bardzo dobry, bardzo blisko). bardzo/bardziej/najbardziej is a three-step ladder on one root, and the very/more confusion is the error this unit exists to prevent - it gets its own slide, two Kontrola items and a Uzycie item. AGREEMENT IS THE ONE GRAMMATICAL FACT: bardziej never changes, the adjective still does. Shown on zmeczony/zmeczona/zmeczone/zmeczeni and chory/chora - EVERY ONE OF THOSE FIVE FORMS IS ALREADY TAUGHT, so the agreement point costs nothing. HOMOGRAPH HELD: zmeczone is TAUGHT <- c1_adj_pl_virile [190] as the NON-VIRILE PLURAL, not as a neuter singular, and it is used here only with Dzieci - its own taught job. zmeczeni likewise stays virile. FENCED, all verified NEW: zajeta, zajete, chore, popularna, popularne (so no agreement-error distractor is possible on List B's masculine-only members - those items use WORD-ORDER errors instead, popularny bardziej), nowoczesna, nowoczesne, skuteczna, skuteczne, zadowolony, znany, interesujacy, tamten - so List B's five non-zmeczony/chory members appear in the MASCULINE ONLY, everywhere, deliberately. mniej + adjective (less tired) is fenced although mniej is TAUGHT <- b1_adverb_comp [126]: it is a second construction and a second decision, and load-splitting says no. Comparison of ADVERBS is b1_adverb_comp's and is never touched. NO FABRICATED NON-WORDS ANYWHERE (spine O12): there is no *zmeczenszy in any distractor. Every wrong choice is real taught Polish in an illegal combination or with the wrong agreement - bardziej dobry, najbardziej duzy, bardzo zmeczona against a masculine subject. NO CASE GOVERNOR IS ADDED, so data/case-map.json is unchanged; niz + Nominative and od + Genitive both ride in unchanged from comparative [26] and superlative [92].

intro.title: Nine adjectives change shape. The rest take a word in front.
intro.body:
The comparative you own is built by changing the adjective itself: dobry becomes lepszy, duży becomes większy. That is nine adjectives, and it has been nine since A1.

Most Polish adjectives do not work that way. They keep their own shape and Polish puts a separate word in front of them: bardziej. The adjective is untouched; only the word in front is new.

This is the second half of a system you have had for four levels. A1 gave you the ending; the other word was held back until there were enough adjectives to use it on.

intro.title: bardzo, bardziej, najbardziej — one root, three steps
intro.body:
You have said bardzo since A2 and it means very: bardzo dobry, bardzo smaczna, bardzo blisko.

bardziej is the same root one step along, and it means more. najbardziej takes the naj- you already put on the nine — najlepszy, najstarszy — and puts it on bardziej instead, giving the most.

The three words look alike and mean three different things. Choosing bardzo where you want bardziej is the commonest mistake here, and it is worth reading the table slowly.

intro.title: bardziej never changes. The adjective still agrees.
intro.body:
bardziej and najbardziej are invariable — one shape, always, for every gender and every number.

The adjective behind them is untouched, which means it goes on agreeing exactly as it did before you met this construction. If you could say Mama jest zmęczona, you can say Mama jest bardziej zmęczona, and nothing else moves.

That is the whole grammar of the unit. Everything else on the remaining slides is about which adjectives take it.

intro.title: Which adjectives take bardziej — two lists, and an honest gap between them
intro.body:
There is a tendency here, and it is worth knowing: adjectives built from verbs — the -ony and -ty shapes you know from participles, like zmęczony and zajęty — take bardziej, and so do several of the longer ones.

But a tendency is not a test, and this course will not hand you one you cannot trust. Polish has plenty of ordinary adjectives that take the ending and are on neither list — trudny gives trudniejszy, not bardziej trudny.

So: learn the two lists. The nine on the left can never take bardziej. The six on the right always do. For any other adjective, look the comparative up rather than building it — the same discipline the prefix unit asked for.

intro.title: najbardziej, and the naj- you already have
intro.body:
The superlative rule does not change: put naj- on the comparative. It is just that here the comparative is a separate word, so naj- lands on bardziej and the adjective is left alone.

The two lists hold for the superlative exactly as they held for the comparative. najlepszy is right and najbardziej dobry is not Polish; najbardziej popularny is right and there is no naj- to put on popularny.

niż and od work here unchanged, which is worth saying plainly: bardziej zmęczony niż mama, bardziej zmęczony od brata. Nothing about the comparison itself is new.

Dad is more tired than my brother.
examples.pl: Tata jest bardziej zmęczony niż brat.

match.en: the most tired · about a man

quiz.explain: bardziej is more. bardzo would say very — the plain adjective with no comparison in it at all.
The word you have had since A2 is bardzo. This item and the one before it are one letter group apart and mean different things.
naj- goes on bardziej, not on the adjective — the adjective is left exactly as it is.
bardziej never changes; the adjective still agrees, so a feminine subject takes zmęczona.
dzieci is not a men-group, so the adjective takes zmęczone — the plural form you met with this noun already. Only the word in front is new.

quiz.prompt: better · dobry is one of the nine →
quiz.explain: dobry builds its comparative by changing the word. bardziej dobry is not Polish — the nine on the left-hand list never take it.

quiz.prompt: bigger · duży is one of the nine →
quiz.explain: Same list, same answer: the word itself changes. bardzo duży is real Polish but it means very big, not bigger.
naj- on the comparative, and dobry's comparative is lepszy. najbardziej lepszy stacks two comparatives on one adjective.

quiz.prompt: more popular · popularny is on the other list →
quiz.explain: popularny has no -szy form to reach for, so the comparative is built with the word in front.

quiz.prompt: This film is the most popular →
quiz.explain: film is masculine, so popularny — and the superlative is carried entirely by najbardziej.
chory is on the bardziej list because it has no comparative ending of its own, and the adjective still agrees: chora.
nowszy is already a comparative — nowy's — so bardziej nowszy would mark it twice. nowoczesny is a different word and takes bardziej.
